record.paper_title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems
record.original_question: Study the discrepancy of explicit Halton-Kronecker sequences, for example the two-dimensional sequence z_n = (x_n, {n sqrt(2)}) where x_n is the one-dimensional Halton sequence in base 2, that is, the van der Corput sequence. The goal is to understand the discrepancy behavior of concrete, not merely metric-almost-all, Halton-Kronecker examples.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 Study the discrepancy of concrete Halton-Kronecker sequences, as for example (xn, {n√2})n≥0 with (xn)n≥0 the van der Corput sequence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $b\ge 2$, the one-dimensional van der Corput sequence in base $b$ is defined by
$$\phi_b(n)=\sum_{j\ge 0} a_j b^{-j-1},\qquad\text{where } n=\sum_{j\ge 0} a_j b^{j},\ a_j\in\{0,1,\dots,b-1\}.$$
Set $x_n=\phi_2(n)$, the binary van der Corput sequence, and consider the two-dimensional Halton–Kronecker sequence
$$z_n=(x_n,\{n\sqrt{2}\})\in[0,1)^2,\qquad n\ge 0,$$
where $\{t\}$ denotes the fractional part of $t\in\mathbb{R}$. The star-discrepancy of the first $N$ points of a sequence $(z_n)$ in $[0,1)^2$ is
$$D_N^*(z)=\sup_{\substack{B=[0,b_1)\times[0,b_2)\\ 0\le b_1,b_2\le 1}}\left|\frac{\#\{0\le n<N:z_n\in B\}}{N}-b_1 b_2\right|.$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $D_N^*(z)$ for this concrete sequence; in particular, find the best possible function $f(N)$ such that
$$N\, D_N^*(z) = O(f(N))\qquad (N\to\infty),$$
and produce matching lower bounds, beyond the metric (almost-all) results known for sequences of the form $(\phi_2(n),\{n\alpha\})$.
artifact.status_search_result: Hofer–Larcher and Drmota have proved upper bounds for the discrepancy of concrete Halton–Kronecker sequences: when α has bounded continued-fraction coefficients (e.g. α=√2), one obtains N D_N^* = O(N^{1/2}(log N)^s), and for algebraic α one has N D_N^* = O(N^{ε}) for every ε>0. Matching sharp asymptotics for the specific sequence (φ_2(n),{n√2}) are not established, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: On the Discrepancy of Halton–Kronecker Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: For α with bounded continued fraction coefficients, ND_N = O(N^{1/2}(log N)^s); for algebraic α, ND_N = O(N^ε).
status_evidence.claim: Concrete upper bounds are known for Halton–Kronecker sequences with specific α such as √2.

status_evidence.title: Metrical results on the discrepancy of Halton–Kronecker sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Metrical (almost-all) discrepancy bounds for Halton–Kronecker sequences.
status_evidence.claim: Prior to concrete bounds, only metric results were available, motivating the open problem.

status_evidence.title: Low Discrepancy Digital Kronecker-Van der Corput Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study discrepancy of digital Kronecker–van der Corput hybrid sequences.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains an active research topic with refinements continuing.
